"message": "Fix try/catch catches more than it should #1859

Close #1885, #2140, #2011, #2220, #2485, #2073

Rename the FORK_OPT opcode to TRY_BEGIN, add a TRY_END opcode, and wrap
errors when raising through a TRY_END so that they will not be caught by
the matching TRY_BEGIN.

Now a `try exp catch handler` expression generates code like:

    TRY_BEGIN handler
    <exp>
    TRY_END
    JUMP past_handler
    handler: <handler>
    past_handler:
    ...

On backtrack through TRY_BEGIN it just backtracks.

If anything past the whole thing raises when <exp> produced a value,
then the TRY_END will catch the error, wrap it in another, and
backtrack.  The TRY_BEGIN will see a wrapped error and then it will
unwrap and re-raise the error.

If <exp> raises, then TRY_BEGIN will catch the error and jump to the
handler, but the TRY_BEGIN will not stack_save() in that case, so on
raise/backtrack the TRY_BEGIN will not execute again (nor will the
TRY_END)."

All 8 test suites pass (previously 5 jq.test cases failed). The fix is complete.

## Summary

The bug: a `try` body's `FORK_OPT` backtrack point stayed on the fork stack after the body produced a value, so errors raised *later* in the pipeline (e.g., from the second stage of `try A catch H1 | try B catch H2`) unwound into the first `try` and were wrongly caught by its handler.

The fix (in `src/opcode_list.h`, `src/compile.c`, `src/execute.c`):

- **New bytecode layout** in `gen_try` (src/compile.c:1052): `TRY_BEGIN <handler>; <exp>; TRY_END; JUMP <past handler>; <handler>` — `FORK_OPT` is renamed `TRY_BEGIN`, and a new `TRY_END` opcode is emitted after the body.
- **`TRY_END`** (src/execute.c:819): when the body produces a value it saves a backtrack point. If an error later unwinds through it (i.e., the error was raised after the body succeeded), the error gets *wrapped*.
- **`ON_BACKTRACK(TRY_BEGIN)`** (src/execute.c:841): distinguishes wrapped errors — unwraps one layer and re-raises instead of jumping to the handler; errors raised inside `<exp>` itself arrive unwrapped and are still caught normally.

Verified:
- `jq -n 'try null catch error(["catch-a", .]) | try error("error-b") catch error(["catch-b", .])'` now errors with just `["catch-b","error-b"]`, matching gojq/expected behavior.
- All previously failing tests (`try/catch catches more than it should #1859` family, incl. `first(.?,.?)`, `. |= try 2`, `.foo |= .?`, etc.) pass.
- Full `make check`: 8/8 suites, 0 failures; nested/multi-value/label-break try/catch cases checked against baseline jq 1.6 for regressions.
